questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Close to home, courses available, academic reputation of the University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UoE made it easy with information before and upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lived in student accommodation so i had RAs, I also had my personal tutor for any academic assistance, and there were many people to contact if i had troubles with anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was very hard and the university accommodation team were very problematic to communicate with during this period. I got my housing offer only one week before going there. 
Housing is generally hard to find in Edinburgh, so I do not have any recommendations. I liked living in student housing but it was stressfull with the late responses.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not really any on campus housing in Edinburgh.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy, they gave you a flyer to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online meeting that guided you before I submitted my application.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesfull and I had my personal tutor afterwards who helped me switch between courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was really good. Comparable to UCPH, but courses were more compressed since the semester is shorter.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very comparable with the lectures, however there was more coursework and their classroom teaching was in much smaller groups at around 10 persons.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mechanisms of Brain Development 3
Immunology 3
Introduction to Social Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Mechanisms of Brain Development 3
Immunology 3
Introduction to Social Anthropology
They were all recommendable, very interesting subjects in all three courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
We had a lot of extra costs for our housing with kitchen utensils and room features. 
We had ordered a university kit from home but the quality was very bad (knifes and pans) and it did not arrive on time so we had to by duvets and sheets ourselves anyway.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I did expect it to be less expensive to go out. It was also more expensive because you often go out a lot when you are abroad compared to home. 
I used around 1500 dkk per month on going out with people for coffee, food and drinks. 
I had all texts provided online, so no expenses on that. 
If you are under 21 you can apply for a free scots card, which give you transportation with busses for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many societies, almost one for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not join any of the societies but i would definitely do it if i went again. There is for example a scandinavian society or societies that arrange diffrent activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to isle of skye! 
There is a company that arrange student tours from Edinburgh and Glasgows, these are better price options and you have other students as your travel companions.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: UoE is not very local. almost only international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Scottish people are very friendly, you can easily ask policeofficers, bus drivers or anybody else for help.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to enjoy it. Use the first weeks when it is still warm to go on tours into the highlands, the last weeks gets more stressed academically. Remember to use some of the many nice study spaces at the university, that helped me a lot.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The extremely beautiful country and Edinburgh is simply stunning. I also liked my courses that really challenged me and was some of the most interesting i have had so far.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Hard to study without the people that are normally part of your study group .

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
